metadata.title: SPARC Horizon threat model and security architecture review — attestation

parties.name: Risk-Sentinel
parties.remarks: The reviewing individual is identified by the verified signature on the commit that introduces this record, not by a name asserted inside it.

metadata.remarks: Horizon's own review, recorded through the evidence chain Horizon builds for everyone else: a hashed back-matter resource, then an observation carrying a native expires. The expiry is what makes this countable by the projection engine rather than a page that quietly ages.

import-ap.remarks: There is no separate assessment plan. The requirement, its scope and its evidencing method are set by docs/dev/issue_rules.md and phase item S0-17 in docs/dev/Implementation_plan.md, which is what this href names. Recorded plainly rather than inventing a plan document to satisfy the field.

results.title: Threat model and security architecture review of the design of record
results.description: Review of docs/01 through docs/10 as of 2026-09-19, before application code exists. Eight findings, recorded in docs/compliance/threat-model.md as TM-1 through TM-8. None is marked mitigated: the design is sound on paper and none of it is enforced yet, which is the correct result for a repository with no application source.

control-selections.description: Developer testing and evaluation — threat modeling and vulnerability analyses.

observations.title: Threat model reviewed and attested
observations.description: The threat model and security architecture review was performed against the design of record and recorded as a dated document. It produced eight findings: one deferred as an open decision (TM-4, the chain head has no anchor outside the writer's control), one accepted and inherited (TM-8, deployment), one accepted risk within TM-5, and the rest carried as requirements on the phases that build the affected component.

relevant-evidence.description: The threat model itself, hashed in back-matter.

observations.remarks: Expiry is 180 days. This observation also goes stale early, before that date, on a change to the trust boundary, the evidence chain order, the signing or canonicalisation scheme, how roles are derived from documents, the isolation of what-if overlays, the federation's peer verification or UUID key grammar, or on the first release serving real projections to an Authorizing Official. Completing a phase is not a trigger: building what the model requires does not invalidate it, changing what it assumed does. The full list is in the Freshness section of the threat model.

resources.title: SPARC Horizon threat model, 2026-09-19
resources.description: The reviewed document. Its hash binds this attestation to that exact text.

resources.title: Process of record — issue_rules.md and phase item S0-17
resources.description: What requires this review, defines its scope, and requires it to be evidenced through the attestation path with freshness asserted.
